met_analysis:
The Well Marked low pressure area over central parts of northern Madhya Pradesh & adjoining south Uttar Pradesh persisted over the same region at 1430 IST of today, the 04th September 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwards with height. It is likely to be quasi-stationary during next 2 days.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level continue to pass through Sri Ganganagar, Narnaul, centre of Well Marked low pressure area over central parts of northern Madhya Pradesh & adjoining south Uttar Pradesh, Daltonganj, Berhampore and thence eastwards towards Tripura.
The trough from Northeast Rajasthan to Manipur across the cyclonic circulation associated with Well Marked low pressure area over central parts of northern Madhya Pradesh & adjoining south Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, north Jharkhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, south Assam extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from south Gujrat to Jharkhand across cyclonic circulation associated with Well Marked low pressure area over central parts of northern Madhya Pradesh & adjoining south Uttar Pradesh and north Chhattisgarh between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over coastal Tamil Nadu & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengalat 7.6 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from South Interior Karnataka to Gulf of Munnar across Tamil Nadu at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle and upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 64°E to the north of Lat. 32°N persists.
